teaching.hint: At amount c, what new combination could a denomination of value exactly c create that smaller denominations could not?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Coins larger than amount c cannot affect its count. Adding coin c contributes exactly one new way at amount c: the single coin by itself. Hence each denomination choice is forced when its own amount is reached.
solution_outline.approach: Maintain standard combination counts from denominations already recovered, starting with one way to make zero. For c from 1 through n, compare the predicted count at c with the supplied count. An equal count means c is absent; a difference of exactly one means c is present and its effects are folded into the count table. Any other difference proves the input impossible.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before considering c, the table counts combinations using exactly the recovered denominations below c. All amounts below c already match the supplied counts and cannot be changed by larger denominations.
solution_outline.correctness: At amount c, no later denomination contributes, while denomination c contributes only its singleton combination. Therefore the comparison determines its presence uniquely or detects inconsistency. The usual unbounded coin update maintains exact combination counts after each chosen denomination. Induction through c=n verifies every supplied amount and yields the only possible sorted set.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n) auxiliary space for n at most 100; each chosen denomination may update all larger amounts.
solution_outline.pitfall: A positive count at amount c does not imply denomination c exists, because smaller coins may already make c.

common_wrong_turns: Choose every denomination with a positive observed count
Treat coin order as making distinct ways
Accept a target count differing by more than one at its own amount
source_fidelity_notes: The long combination table was omitted; 1-based amount indexing, order-insensitive combinations inferred from examples, unlimited distinct denominations, bounds, and empty-result behavior were stated explicitly.
